newsitem.title: USA: CBOT to meet with Born on grain storage capacity.
newsitem.headline: CBOT to meet with Born on grain storage capacity.

text.p: Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) officials will meet with Brooksley Born, chairperson of the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), on Tuesday, to discuss expanding grain storage capacity outlined in the CBOT's corn and soybean futures contracts.

"We are committed to addressing this problem," CBOT chairman Patrick Arbor said at a news briefing before he and CBOT president Thomas Donovan embark on a two-day trip to Washington to meet with regulatory officials and legislators.
The CFTC said on December 19 that the delivery terms of the CBOT's corn and soybean contracts no longer met the statutory objectives in the Commodity Exchange Act (CEA).
The CFTC also expressed concerns about the potential for market manipulation, and ordered the CBOT to submit a plan to raise the capacity and number of locations for grain delivery.
"I haven't had any direct communication from them (CFTC) about any urgent problems," Arbor said in response to questions about the current potential for price manipulation.
The CBOT must submit a plan to the CFTC by mid-March.
He said CBOT directors will appoint a task force to review regular grain storage capacity at Wednesday's board meeting.

While trade in CBOT's corn and soybean futures contracts has grown eight-fold since the early 1970s, elevator storage in the vicinity has declined, according to statements made by CFTC commissioner Barbara Holum on December 19.
"We now face a situation where the contracts have a combined open interest of three billion bushels and storage capacity somewhere in the vicinity of 15 million bushels," she said.
In October 1996, members of the CBOT rejected a proposal to allow corn, soybeans and wheat to be delivered against futures in Chicago, Toledo, Milwaukee and at points along the Illinois River.
The plan would have also eliminated St Louis as a delivery point.
Arbor said the task force committee would probably take another look at those proposals.

"I would not be surprised to see some of those in the final recommendation," Arbor said, adding that CBOT members would have to vote on a final proposal. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com))
